articles.title: India Just Killed the Physical OCI Booklet. Five Million Cardholders Can Finally Exhale.
articles.excerpt: The new e-OCI card lets overseas Indians complete the entire OCI lifecycle on a phone — no consular visits, no duplicate paperwork, no reissue anxiety.
articles.image_caption: Union Home Minister Amit Shah, who launched the e-OCI Card system in New Delhi
articles.nri_angle: Eliminates the single biggest bureaucratic pain point for 5M+ OCI holders worldwide — the mandatory physical booklet reissue that required consular visits, mailed documents, and weeks of waiting every time a passport was renewed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Leicester's South Asian Arts Festival Turns Fifteen. The City Barely Notices — It Has Been Living This for Decades.
articles.excerpt: An Indian Summer returns to Leicester Cathedral, Jubilee Square, and Attenborough Arts Centre this week with five days of theatre, music, film, and dance.
articles.image_caption: A traditional South Asian dancer performs on stage in vibrant costume and accessories
articles.nri_angle: Highlights how Leicester's concentrated South Asian diaspora sustains a 15-year-old contemporary arts festival — a model for diaspora cultural institutions that create shared physical space for identity beyond streaming and WhatsApp groups.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Supreme Court Just Ruled 6-3 That Children of H-1B Parents Born in America Are Citizens. No President Can Change That.
articles.excerpt: In a landmark ruling, the conservative-majority court struck down Trump's executive order targeting birthright citizenship — a decision that Indian American advocacy groups are calling 'a profound affirmation of who belongs in America.'
articles.image_caption: The United States Supreme Court in Washington, D.C.
articles.nri_angle: Indian families on H-1B and L-1 visas, who face the longest green card backlogs in the system, now have Supreme Court confirmation that their U.S.-born children's citizenship is constitutionally protected.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: America Turns 250. The Indian Diaspora Is Celebrating with Both Flags.
articles.excerpt: From a packed curtain raiser in Mineola to a tall ship in Baltimore Harbour, Indian Americans are weaving their story into the semiquincentennial — while already rehearsing for India's 80th.
articles.image_caption: The annual India Day Parade in New York City — Indian Americans celebrate their dual identity as America marks its 250th (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: The Indian-American community is uniquely positioned this summer, celebrating America's 250th birthday while preparing for India's 80th Independence Day — a dual-calendar life that defines the diaspora experience.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Bay Area Temples Hit in Three Weeks. The Diaspora Is Running Out of Cheeks to Turn.
articles.excerpt: Pro-Khalistan graffiti at a Swaminarayan mandir, a copycat attack in Hayward, and a burglary at a third temple have shaken Silicon Valley's Indian-American heartland — and renewed a question the community has never been able to put down.
articles.image_caption: A BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in California, similar to the temples targeted in the Bay Area attacks
articles.nri_angle: The Bay Area temple attacks strike at the heart of the Indian-American community's sense of belonging — raising the question of whether success and visibility have made the diaspora a target rather than a shield.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Diaspora's Highest-Ranking AI Voice in Washington Just Walked Out of the White House
articles.excerpt: Sriram Krishnan's six-month run as Trump's senior AI policy adviser ends today. He's not done with Washington — he's just changing the address.
articles.image_caption: Sriram Krishnan, who served as senior White House AI policy adviser
articles.nri_angle: Krishnan's trajectory from Chennai to the West Wing represents a new frontier for Indian-American influence — policy, not just corporate leadership — and his departure raises the question of who fills the gap.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: He Sent ₹11 Lakh to His Parents. India's Tax Department Took Six Years to Believe It Was a Gift.
articles.excerpt: A US-based NRI's routine family transfer turned into a protracted legal battle. The case is a masterclass in what every diaspora family sending money home gets wrong.
articles.image_caption: The Income Tax Department of India — NRI remittances can trigger scrutiny if not properly documented (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs send money to family in India every year with minimal documentation. This case shows exactly how that can go wrong — and what to do about it.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi and Carney Have Met Four Times in Under a Year. Here's What India and Canada Just Agreed To.
articles.excerpt: A C$2.6 billion uranium deal, a defence pact, a free trade agreement by December, and 300 research scholarships — the India-Canada relationship has turned around so fast that neither side seems sure what to do with the momentum.
articles.image_caption: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, who has met PM Modi four times in under a year
articles.nri_angle: Canada is home to 1.8 million Indian-origin people — the diplomatic reset directly affects visa processing, education pathways, business opportunities, and community safety for the largest Indian diaspora outside the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Five Indian Americans, Five Fields, One State: Inside GOPIO-CT's 20th Anniversary Honours
articles.excerpt: A state senator, a nanotech founder, a journalist, a bank CEO, and an engineering professor — Connecticut's diaspora organisation celebrated two decades by showcasing the community's breadth.
articles.image_caption: Indian Americans celebrating community achievements — GOPIO-CT has been building diaspora institutions in Connecticut for two decades (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: GOPIO-CT's 20th anniversary banquet in Darien honoured five Indian American leaders spanning politics, biotech, journalism, banking, and engineering — illustrating the community's growing institutional depth and bipartisan political standing in the American Northeast.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Rate War for NRI Dollars: Indian Banks Are Offering Up to 7.5% on Foreign Currency Deposits
articles.excerpt: The RBI removed interest rate ceilings and is subsidising hedging costs until September 30. Banks have responded with the most aggressive FCNR repricing in years. Here's what it means for your money.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai, which triggered a bank-level rate war with its June FCNR policy changes
articles.nri_angle: A practical guide for NRIs weighing the best FCNR deposit rates after the RBI's unprecedented June 2026 policy changes — comparing bank-by-bank offers, tax treatment, lock-in terms, and the September 30 deadline that makes this a limited-time opportunity.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Passport Fees Jump Up to 75% From July 1. Here’s What Changes for NRIs.
articles.excerpt: The Ministry of External Affairs has revised passport charges across the board — fresh applications, renewals, Tatkaal, and replacements all cost more. With 32 million overseas Indians, the timing is hard to ignore.
articles.image_caption: An Indian passport. Fee revisions notified by the Ministry of External Affairs take effect on July 1, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: India's 32 million overseas Indians rely on passport services for travel, residency, and legal identity. The fee hike affects Gulf renewals, family applications, and consular services worldwide. Paired with broader July 1 financial changes including ITR deadline shifts and credit card reporting rules.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Belfast Burned. An Indian Woman Fed the Families Left Behind.
articles.excerpt: Anti-immigration riots in Northern Ireland displaced dozens of minority families. For the Indian community in the UK, the violence has deepened a quiet unease about safety that no advisory can fully address.
articles.image_caption: Belfast City Hall, Donegall Square — the heart of a city shaken by anti-immigration violence in June 2026. (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: The Belfast riots forced Indians and other ethnic minorities in Northern Ireland to confront their vulnerability. Ruchira Rangaprasad's community meal drive and INSIGHT UK's safety advisory for Hindu communities reflect a diaspora learning to protect itself in an increasingly hostile European landscape.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Diaspora's Philanthropy Machine Just Turned 25. It Raised a Record $3.8 Million in One Night.
articles.excerpt: The American India Foundation's silver-jubilee gala honoured BNY, Bharat Masrani and Salil Parekh — and marked a turning point for Indian-American giving that has nearly tripled in six years.
articles.image_caption: Bharat Masrani, retired CEO of TD Bank Group, was honoured at AIF's 25th-anniversary gala at Cipriani Wall Street
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American philanthropy has reached an inflection point, with giving tripling to $4–5 billion and the gap between potential and actual donations shrinking to $1 billion. AIF's gala channels that energy into education, health and livelihoods across India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: She Built the Middleware That Moves Indian Brands Across Borders. EY Just Noticed.
articles.excerpt: Somdutta Singh becomes the third and youngest Indian woman to win an EY Entrepreneur Of The Year award, after Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw and Falguni Nayar.
articles.image_caption: Somdutta Singh, founder and CEO of Assiduus, is just the third Indian woman to win the EY Entrepreneur Of The Year Southeast award (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Singh's cross-border commerce platform is the infrastructure layer NRIs and Indian exporters depend on. Her recognition at a global entrepreneurship award elevates the visibility of Indian women founders in the diaspora business landscape.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Indian Law Graduate Just Became CFO of America's Biggest Gym Chain. He Also Runs Its Global Expansion.
articles.excerpt: Planet Fitness appoints Sudhanshu Priyadarshi — a National Law School alumnus who has steered finances at Keurig, PepsiCo, and Walmart — as CFO and President, International.
articles.image_caption: A Planet Fitness location in Ypsilanti Township, Michigan — part of the chain's 2,700-strong network that Priyadarshi now helps steer
articles.nri_angle: Priyadarshi's appointment at Planet Fitness extends the growing pattern of Indian-origin executives reaching the C-suite of major American consumer brands, normalising a career trajectory that was rare a generation ago.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
